name: Nutrients
blurb: Vitamin D, iron, omega-3 and vitamin K

claims.claim: Breastfed infants require vitamin D supplementation
claims.testedAs: Vitamin D supplementation in breastfed infants reduces vitamin D deficiency and rickets

nhs.says: Give breastfed babies a daily vitamin D supplement of 8.5 to 10 micrograms from birth to age 1. Formula-fed babies on 500ml a day do not need one.

aap.says: Give breastfed and partly breastfed babies 400 IU of vitamin D a day, starting in the first few days of life.

claims.query: vitamin D supplementation breastfed infant deficiency

claims.claim: Omega-3 DHA intake in infancy supports brain and visual development
claims.testedAs: Omega-3 DHA intake in infancy supports brain and visual development

aap.says: DHA and ARA, added to most formulas, are believed to matter for a baby's brain and eye development.

claims.query: DHA omega 3 infant brain visual development supplementation

claims.claim: Iron-rich complementary foods are needed from 6 months
claims.testedAs: Iron-rich complementary foods from 6 months lead to better health outcomes

nhs.says: Once solids start at around 6 months, include iron-containing foods such as meat, fish, fortified cereals, beans and greens.

aap.says: Iron-rich foods from about 6 months supply the extra iron babies need for growth.

claims.query: iron rich complementary food infant 6 months stores depletion

claims.claim: Vitamin K at birth prevents haemorrhagic disease of the newborn
claims.testedAs: Vitamin K at birth prevents haemorrhagic disease of the newborn

nhs.says: Your baby will be offered a vitamin K injection after birth. It prevents haemorrhagic disease of the newborn, a rare bleeding disorder.

aap.says: Every newborn should get a vitamin K shot at birth. One injection protects your baby from vitamin K deficiency bleeding.
